title: [Bug] ttnn.repeat_bw TT_FATALs on non-tile-multiple shapes, returns an empty gradient list for a dim-2/dim-3 repeat, and a whole-axis sum when the repeated dim's extent is > 1
body:
### Describe the bug

`ttnn.repeat_bw` fails on three whole classes of input that the forward `ttnn.repeat` handles fine:

1. **It raises `TT_FATAL` for any input whose last two logical dims are not multiples of 32.** `(1, 1, 17, 37)` with `sizes = [2, 1, 1, 1]` aborts inside `moreh_sum`, although `ttnn.repeat` on the very same tensor is bit-exact against `torch.Tensor.repeat`.
2. **It silently returns an empty gradient list for a repeat along dim 2 or dim 3**, with no exception and no warning — even for a fully tile-aligned `(1, 1, 32, 32)` input. `ttnn.repeat_bw(grad, x, [1, 1, 2, 1])` returns `[]`.
3. **It silently returns a wrong-shaped gradient when the repeated dim's extent is bigger than 1.** `(1, 3, 32, 32)` with `sizes = [1, 2, 1, 1]` returns a `(1, 1, 32, 32)` tensor where `torch` gives `(1, 3, 32, 32)`: the whole axis is summed instead of the 2 tiled blocks.

All three come from [`unary_backward.cpp#L1590-L1640`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary_backward/unary_backward.cpp#L1590-L1640):

* L1599 takes `auto shape_wh = input.padded_shape();` and L1612 / L1628 build the preallocated `moreh_sum` output from it (`ttnn::zeros({1, shape_wh[1], shape_wh[2], shape_wh[3]}, ...)`). moreh validates a preallocated output against the **logical** dims of the reduction result ([`moreh_helper_functions.cpp#L401`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/moreh/moreh_helper_functions.cpp#L401)), so a padded shape is rejected: `Input dimension without padding[0] (37) must equal output dimension without padding[0] (64)`.
* The function only has branches for `shape[0] > 1` (L1609) and `shape[1] > 1` (L1624). A repeat on dim 2 or dim 3 falls through to the trailing `return grad_tensor;` at L1639 with nothing ever pushed into the vector.
* Both branches reduce the whole axis with `moreh_sum`. `x.repeat(sizes)` tiles the axis in `sizes[dim]` blocks of the input's extent, so the gradient is the sum of those blocks; a full reduction only coincides with it when the extent is 1. Dim 0 is safe (L1600 requires `input.shape[0] == 1`), dim 1 is not guarded.

The registered golden ([`unary_backward.py#L944`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/ttnn/operations/unary_backward.py#L944)) is `torch` autograd over `input_tensor.repeat(sizes)` and returns a gradient with the input's shape for every one of the four dims, and the binding docstring promises `List of ttnn.Tensor: the output tensor`, so all three cases are in-contract.

### Repro

```python
import torch, ttnn

device = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0)

def tt(x):
    return ttnn.from_torch(x, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT, device=device)

# (2) empty gradient list, tile-aligned input, no error raised
x = torch.randn(1, 1, 32, 32).bfloat16()
g = torch.randn(1, 1, 64, 32).bfloat16()
print(ttnn.repeat_bw(tt(g), tt(x), [1, 1, 2, 1]))     # []  (torch returns a (1,1,32,32) grad)

# (3) wrong shape, silently: the whole axis is summed instead of the 2 blocks
x = torch.randn(1, 3, 32, 32).bfloat16()
g = torch.randn(1, 6, 32, 32).bfloat16()
print(ttnn.repeat_bw(tt(g), tt(x), [1, 2, 1, 1])[0].shape)   # Shape([1, 1, 32, 32]), torch: [1, 3, 32, 32]

# (1) TT_FATAL for a non-tile-multiple input the forward op accepts
x = torch.randn(1, 1, 17, 37).bfloat16()
print(ttnn.repeat(tt(x), [2, 1, 1, 1]).shape)         # Shape([2, 1, 17, 37])  - forward is fine
g = torch.randn(2, 1, 17, 37).bfloat16()
ttnn.repeat_bw(tt(g), tt(x), [2, 1, 1, 1])
# RuntimeError: TT_FATAL @ ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/moreh/moreh_helper_functions.cpp:401:
#   input_dim_wo_padding[i] == output_dim_wo_padding[i]
#   info: Input dimension without padding[0] (37) must equal output dimension without padding[0] (64)
```

### Observed vs expected

bfloat16 (the only dtype `repeat_bw` documents), `TILE_LAYOUT`, ttsim Blackhole, `grad` and `input` from `torch.randn`. `maxULP` is the largest bfloat16 ULP distance between the returned gradient and the float64 golden; where nothing usable is returned there is no value to measure.

| input shape | sizes | observed | expected | maxULP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (1, 1, 32, 32) | [2, 1, 1, 1] | (1, 1, 32, 32) gradient | (1, 1, 32, 32) gradient | 1 |
| (1, 1, 32, 64) | [2, 1, 1, 1] | (1, 1, 32, 64) gradient | (1, 1, 32, 64) gradient | 1 |
| (1, 1, 17, 32) | [2, 1, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (17 vs 32) | (1, 1, 17, 32) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 32, 17) | [2, 1, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (17 vs 32) | (1, 1, 32, 17) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 33, 32) | [2, 1, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (33 vs 64) | (1, 1, 33, 32) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 32, 33) | [2, 1, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (33 vs 64) | (1, 1, 32, 33) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 17, 37) | [2, 1, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (37 vs 64) | (1, 1, 17, 37) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 7, 7) | [4, 1, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (7 vs 32) | (1, 1, 7, 7) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 33, 65) | [4, 1, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (65 vs 96) | (1, 1, 33, 65) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 17, 37) | [1, 3, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (37 vs 64) | (1, 1, 17, 37) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 7, 7) | [1, 24, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (7 vs 32) | (1, 1, 7, 7) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 32, 32) | [1, 1, 2, 1] | `[]` | (1, 1, 32, 32) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 32, 32) | [1, 1, 1, 2] | `[]` | (1, 1, 32, 32) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 17, 37) | [1, 1, 3, 1] | `[]` | (1, 1, 17, 37) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 17, 37) | [1, 1, 1, 3] | `[]` | (1, 1, 17, 37) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 320, 384) | [1, 1, 1, 2] | `[]` | (1, 1, 320, 384) gradient | no result |
| (1, 1, 7, 7) | [1, 1, 1, 1] | `[]` | (1, 1, 7, 7) gradient (= grad) | no result |
| (1, 3, 32, 32) | [1, 2, 1, 1] | (1, **1**, 32, 32) whole-axis sum | (1, 3, 32, 32) gradient | wrong shape |
| (1, 2, 17, 37) | [1, 3, 1, 1] | `TT_FATAL` (37 vs 64), and a (1, **1**, 17, 37) whole-axis sum once case 1 is fixed | (1, 2, 17, 37) gradient | no result |

Forward control in the same run — `ttnn.repeat` is **bit-exact** against `torch.Tensor.repeat` at `(1, 1, 17, 37)` for `[2,1,1,1]`, `[1,2,1,1]`, `[1,1,2,1]` and `[1,1,1,2]`, and at `(1, 3, 32, 32)` for `[1,2,1,1]`. Only the backward op rejects or mishandles those shapes.

### Affected range

* Case 1: every input in `TILE_LAYOUT` whose logical H or W is not a multiple of 32, for repeats on dim 0 or dim 1 — i.e. every sub-tile and every ragged shape. Tile-multiple shapes are unaffected.
* Case 2: every repeat on dim 2 or dim 3, at any shape, tile-aligned or not, including the no-op `[1, 1, 1, 1]`. That is half of the op's parameter space. `tests/ttnn/profiling/ops_for_profiling.py:209` calls `ttnn.repeat_bw(x, y, shape=(1, 1, 1, 4))`, i.e. straight into this path.
* Case 3: every repeat on dim 1 of an input whose dim 1 is not 1.

### Expected behavior

`ttnn.repeat_bw(grad, input, sizes)` should return one gradient with the input's shape for every `sizes` the forward `ttnn.repeat` accepts, matching the registered golden (`torch` autograd over `input.repeat(sizes)`): the sum of the `sizes[dim]` tiled blocks along the repeated axis.

### Why CI does not catch this

`tests/ttnn/nightly/unit_tests/operations/eltwise/backward/test_backward_repeat.py` parametrises `sizes` over `[12,1,1,1]`, `[6,1,1,1]`, `[1,24,1,1]`, `[1,3,1,1]` only — never dim 2 or dim 3 — and only over `[1,1,32,32]` and `[1,1,320,384]`: both tile multiples, and both with a dim-1 extent of 1. It would also not fail if it did cover them: `compare_pcc` loops over the returned list, so an empty list passes vacuously, and it never checks the gradient's shape. The regression test in the fix PR asserts the list length and the shape before comparing.

### Which architectures

Both. `repeat_bw` is a host-side composite in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary_backward/unary_backward.cpp`; there is no per-arch kernel involved, so Wormhole and Blackhole behave identically.

### How it was verified

ttsim Blackhole v1.10.6 (`TT_METAL_SIMULATOR=libttsim_bh.so`, `TT_METAL_SLOW_DISPATCH_MODE=1`), bfloat16, `TILE_LAYOUT`, golden = `torch` autograd over `input.repeat(sizes)` in float64 (the registered golden's own formula). The forward `ttnn.repeat` was run on the same tensors in the same session as a control.
